description: The creator listed as B, Britt publishes a Python Monte Carlo simulator of correlated supply-chain disruption risks. Supplier failure can influence transport delay, while log-normal cost distributions represent heavy-tailed losses. The described outputs include financial loss, service-level degradation, expected values and 95 and 99 percent value-at-risk estimates. Command-line parameters select sample count, correlation, random seed and optional visualisation. Zenodo distributes the December 2025 version 1.0 archive free under MIT. NumPy and SciPy are required; Matplotlib is needed only for plotting. The model is not calibrated to a named country, supplier network or observation period, and its probability and cost assumptions need checking for any application. Reuse is as a transparent statistical baseline for disruption scenarios, not evidence of a real firm's risk. No related catalogue model is explicitly identified.
